frequency_question: What proportion of major federal voter eligibility bills passing one chamber successfully pass the U.S. Senate with exact identity-verification criteria intact before the deadline?
membership_rule: Members are federal bills requiring documentary proof of citizenship for voter registration that receive floor consideration; excluded are non-binding resolutions, state-level bills, and bills lacking specific citizenship documentation mandates.
provenance_note: 3 cases named, 4 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.3x); rate of 0% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 distinct legislative attempts or cycles identified where strict documentary proof bills were advanced.
known_gaps: Some minor committee-level amendments may have omitted strict documentation definitions.
skeleton: Total major restrictive voter registration legislative push cycles since 1995 (n=4) multiplied by Senate passage rate under specific procedural thresholds.
validity_reason: Valid until the expiration of the current congressional session structure.
